exposure: arrest of descent in the second stage of labor
cohort: The study retrospectively reviewed delivery records of 18,508 women, with cases being 123 women with singleton vertex pregnancy and unscarred uterus who had an arrest of descent in the second stage of labor, and controls being women who delivered vaginally without arrest of descent.
finding: Arrest of descent occurred in 44 per 1000 births and was significantly associated with nulliparity, prelabor rupture of membranes, birth weight >3000g, doubtful pelvic adequacy, and large caput, leading to higher rates of postpartum hemorrhage, postnatal fever, and NICU admission.
mod_finding: The presence of a large caput was the only significantly associated factor (OR: 6.429, P = 0.002) predicting cesarean delivery in women with arrest of descent.
